reviews.text:
We stopped by by chance on our way to Kaiyukan. A Korean staff member explained everything very kindly, and the kids really loved the hands-on experience (Hercules beetles, stag beetles, etc.).

It was 1,000 yen per person, so I highly recommend visiting if you have children who like insects.

As my child was heading to the checkout counter with a toy, the store clerk laughed and said, "Don't touch the merchandise without permission."
How am I supposed to buy it?

What a strange store clerk.
My child really loved being able to see a variety of live beetles that cannot be seen in Korea.
Really cool place! Got to explore this place if you come to the Kaiyukan area, lots of varieties for beetles and foodstuffs for pet insects as well.
That's great. The insects are fascinating.

An absolute delight. Paid 1000 yen to hold 3 huge beetles! Staff is so friendly and the swag is so cute. Highly recommend if you don’t have time to go to the Minoh Insectarium and are only in Osaka for a little while!

The staff didn't even greet me; the customer service was terrible.
I came all the way here hoping to get some advice, but I lost all interest in buying a pet and left immediately.
Please treat new customers with care.
I will never go there again.

This is a place my child was really looking forward to.

It was great to be able to see and touch the special insects up close.

However, the staff service was a bit disappointing.

It definitely looked like the owner... haha.

We went there even though we had given up on visiting the aquarium... haha.

My child liked it, but I'm left with a lot of regrets.

We stumbled upon an insect shop on our way to the subway after visiting Kaiyukan. It was filled with stag beetles and rhinoceros beetles. The hands-on experience costs 1,000 yen per person. I visited without high expectations, but I was surprised by how much the kids loved it. It felt like my memories of visiting Kaiyukan were completely reset. On top of that, the owner is Korean, so they explained everything in detail in Korean and were incredibly kind. If you are touring Kaiyukan, you should definitely visit. The kids absolutely loved it!
